Dermal disease umbrella; skin defects are shared, while extracutaneous abnormalities vary among syndromic subtypes.
Congenital bilateral absence or hypoplasia of the tibiae.
Fatty-acid oxidation defect; decreased liver function occurs in 30-79%. Myopathy and lasting neurologic injury are minority features; weakness alone does not establish muscle damage.

Acute middle-ear effusion and inflammation; nonsuppurative disease does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.
Vaginal inflammation has no anatomical axis. This umbrella explicitly includes noninfectious disease; infection is not established by the generic diagnosis.

Atrial electrical rhythm disorder; thromboembolism is a separate complication rather than defining organ involvement.
Defining skeletal, ectodermal and cardiac defects; dental/oral abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Cap excludes reported renal and pulmonary anomalies (30-79%).
Static cerebral injury produces hemidystonia with ipsilateral body and limb atrophy; both neurologic dysfunction and hemiatrophy define the syndrome.
Occlusion of the female genital tract; reproductive structures have no axis.
Renal dysplasia or agenesis, congenital cardiac malformations and cleft lip/palate define the syndrome; oral structures belong to gastrointestinal.
Lymphatic vessel dilatation is a vascular disorder; pulmonary disease belongs to a specific subtype rather than the entire umbrella.
Ovarian endocrine dysfunction with hyperandrogenism and ovulatory disturbance; hirsutism does not establish skin damage, and diabetes is a separate disease.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and progressive orthopedic deformities define it. Cardiac and urinary malformations each occur in 30-79%; ocular abnormalities omitted under the cap.
Carcinoma originates in the endometrium, a reproductive structure outside the axes; no common direct involvement of another axis is established.
Malignant adipocytic mesenchymal soft-tissue tumor; origin is not restricted to skin or subcutis.
Immunodeficiency defined by defective neutrophil phagocytosis and migration; both immune function and blood-cell function are intrinsically affected.
Inherited epidermal keratinization disorder with epidermolysis and ichthyotic hyperkeratosis.
Apolipoprotein misfolding/deposition disorder; renal impairment occurs in 80-99%. Cardiac amyloid is only 1-4%; common ventricular dysfunction alone does not prove direct cardiac deposition.
Intracranial arterial aneurysm is a vessel disorder; brain injury from rupture is not established as common or defining for this concept.
Primary microcephaly with universal intellectual disability and frequent cortical developmental abnormalities; extracranial findings do not meet the involvement threshold.
